$comment: Read from Google's own discovery document, not docs prose: documents.create -> POST v1/documents, request Document, response Document. The method creates a BLANK document and ignores every request field except title, including any supplied content.
title: Google Docs document
description: Create a blank Google Docs document.
$idempotencyComment: Google offers no idempotency key on documents.create -- the discovery method declares no parameters and no idempotency header. So this is honestly unsafe-to-replay with no way to make it safe: a retried durable run creates a SECOND document.

config.label: Title
config.description: The title of the new blank document.
config.$comment: Document is a large response schema, but create is not a way to seed one. Google's method says all request fields other than title -- including content -- are ignored, so exposing a body or tabs field would accept configuration that can never work.

outputShape.description: The id of the created document.

$outputComment: The Document is returned at the HTTP response top level. The connector runtime places that body under `data`; there is no provider-specific wrapper such as `{document: ...}`.

contract.$comment: The exact Document properties this action sends and reads. Drift-check projects these names from the discovery schema instead of treating the endpoint as unresearched.
